label: QSFP28 50GBASE-LR 10 km
notes: IEEE 802.3cd-2018 Clause 139 (Tables 139-6 and 139-7, 50GBASE-LR column): one 26.5625 GBd PAM4 carrier at 1311 nm over a 1304.5-1317.5 nm window, duplex LC, 10 km on G.652, RS(544,514) KP4 FEC required. Average launch power -4.5..+4.2 dBm and average receive power -10.8..+4.2 dBm, receiver sensitivity in OMA -8.4 dBm, stressed receiver sensitivity -5.1 dBm OMA. FS QSFP28-LR-50G, Gigalight GSS-SPO500-LR1Z, AddOn QSFP-50GB-LR1-AO and Huawei OSL010N01 print the same launch and receive averages, which is what makes the row re-checkable. Read the class's 10.3 dB power budget carefully: it is 6.3 dB of channel insertion loss plus a 4.0 dB allowance for the PAM4 eye (TDECQ), and because the engine compares average launch with average receive, -4.5 - (-10.8) = 6.3 is the whole figure a link may spend - the same arithmetic as 25GBASE-LR and 100GBASE-LR1. Consequence at the default 3 dB margin: 10 km x 0.35 dB/km = 3.5 dB of fibre leaves 2.8 dB and reads fail, and it is the margin that refuses it, not the 10 km of reach; the last length that clears the margin is 9.43 km bare (3.3 / 0.35) and 7.71 km with a patch-panel pair (2.7 / 0.35); ok, which needs 5 dB of headroom, begins at 3.71 km bare ((6.3 - 5) / 0.35 = 3.714) or 2.0 km with the pair ((6.3 - 0.6 - 5) / 0.35). Launch ceiling +4.2 dBm equals the receiver maximum +4.2, so a back-to-back pair sits exactly on the overload point and two matings take it 0.6 dB clear, which is why this row needs no pad - the opposite of 50GBASE-ER. One carrier at 1310 nm, so nothing here is a worst-lane hand-wave: it is a 50G row, and budget.pointToPoint refuses it against a 25G or 100G optic on speed, the check the four-lane rows cannot give. Class figures from the clause, not one measured module: replace the row with the module actually purchased before pricing a build.
